summary: RuleCases C-001 and C-003 no longer hard-code a settled count. A new lazy, memoised Get-ExpectedSettled in tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1 counts every item of the rules: list in .taad/fitness.yaml and subtracts the 15 twinned entries the AGREE line pins. C-001 builds its full expected line from that number and C-003 expects that number plus one. The oracle never reads rules-parity output and never counts per '# settled by' marker. Case-C007 is left untouched, following the O-015 decision. A permanent probe, tests/rules/SettledCountProbe.ps1, puts each growth and bite shape into a scratch copy under both shells, plus the guard-rule check. Everything passes: C-001 and C-003 under both shells, all nine probe shapes, the whole RuleCases suite with the engine (all 14 cases), and the engine's Fitness check on the fixed tree (48 rules, 0 violations).

files.why: Adds $Twinned = 15 and a lazy, memoised Get-ExpectedSettled: a line-by-line count of the rules: list items in .taad/fitness.yaml, minus the twinned entries. It throws 'ExpectedSettled: fitness rule count unavailable: ...' or 'ExpectedSettled: derived count <n> < 1 (...)'. C-001's literal '28 settled' and its hand-kept tally comment are replaced by the derived count. C-003's literal '29 settled' becomes (Get-ExpectedSettled) + 1, computed from this repo's own yaml before the copy is appended to. Case-C007 is unchanged.

The growth-and-bite probe, made permanent so the engine can run one command per case obligation. Shapes: AppendOne, AppendTwo, CountPlusOne, NotAgree, Misclassified, C003Base, OracleUnavailable, BothShells, GuardRule. Each copies the four files C-001 and C-003 read into %TEMP%, changes one thing, and runs that copy's RuleCases.ps1 under powershell.exe and pwsh, checking the exit code and output.

Not edited by this build. The engine appended the SL-053 guard rule ('# settled by SL-053', 'the rule-case suite never pins a literal settled-entry count') at design acceptance. It was already modified in the working tree when the build started.

obligations.how: `RuleCases.ps1 -Case C-001` on the current tree, which already includes SL-053's own settled entry (33 settled, more than the survey's 32). It exits 0 under both pwsh and powershell.exe, with 8 ok checks, with and without -ExpectFacts 11. The expected line reads '...27 patterns; 33 settled entries not compared'.
SettledCountProbe -Shape AppendOne appends one engine-shaped settled entry below a new marker in a scratch copy. C-001 exits 0 under both shells and prints base+1 (34).
SettledCountProbe -Shape AppendTwo appends two entries under a single '# settled by SL-998' marker. C-001 exits 0 under both shells with base+2 (35), so a per-marker count would have failed.

SettledCountProbe -Shape CountPlusOne changes the scratch copy's eng/rules-parity.ps1:633 to print $yaml.Settled + 1. C-001 exits 1 with exactly '4 check(s) failed.' (the four 'says' checks; exit codes still hold). The bite was measured separately: an oracle read from the tool's own output makes this shape fail the probe.
SettledCountProbe -Shape NotAgree changes the AGREE line to print 'rules-parity: DRIFT' with identical counts and exit 0. C-001 exits 1 with '4 check(s) failed.' under both shells.

SettledCountProbe -Shape Misclassified makes the tool print 14 twinned and settled+1. C-001 exits 1 with '4 check(s) failed.' under both shells. The oracle subtracts the pinned $Twinned (15), not the tool's figure. An expected line read back from the tool made this shape fail the probe (measured).

SettledCountProbe -Shape C003Base: on an unchanged copy, C-003 exits 0 and expects base+1 (34), taken from the copy's own unappended yaml. With the tool mutated not to move (settled-1) or to move by two (settled+1), C-003 exits 1 with 'FAIL  the same entry appended below the marker' and '2 check(s) failed.' under both shells. A tool-reading oracle fails this probe (measured).

SettledCountProbe -Shape OracleUnavailable, in lone -Case runs under both shells. With the yaml deleted, C-001 prints its header and then 'C-001 stopped: ExpectedSettled: fitness rule count unavailable', exit 1. With a yaml cut to its 15 twinned entries, C-001 fails with 'ExpectedSettled: derived count 0 < 1', exit 1. On that same yaml, C-002 exits 0 with 'All checks held.' and never mentions ExpectedSettled, so evaluation is lazy and confined to the cases that ask for it.

SettledCountProbe -Shape BothShells runs C-001 under powershell.exe and pwsh on the full yaml (33 settled) and on one cut to exactly one settled entry. All exit 0 with '; 1 settled entries' on the cut yaml. Every other shape also runs under both shells. The oracle counts with an [int] counter in a for loop and uses no pipeline, so there is no scalar or array unrolling.

RuleCases -Case C-007 with -EnginePython %APPDATA%\taad3\venv\Scripts\python.exe and -EngineRoot taad_v3\backend exits 0 in 52 s: 'the Fitness rule count equals the yaml entries (twinned + settled)' holds. A direct Fitness run gives 48 rules = 15 twinned + 33 settled, which equals Get-ExpectedSettled's count of rules: items (48). C-007 itself was not modified (O-015).

SettledCountProbe -Shape GuardRule reads the rule's pattern from .taad/fitness.yaml by name. It hits the pre-fix RuleCases.ps1 (git show 0647ead) at exactly 205,268, and nothing in the current file. It also hits literal samples and misses the interpolated forms and C-007's '(\d+) settled' regex. The engine's own Fitness check agrees: before the fix, verdict fail with hits at tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1:205 and :268; after it, verdict pass with 0 violations.

Measured, though owed to validate-slice. Per O-015 the oracle is no longer Fitness's rule count but a direct count of rules: items in .taad/fitness.yaml. That count (48) equals Fitness's rule count (48) and parity's twinned + settled (15 + 33), and C-007 is green on this tree, so the premise twinned + settled = rule count holds.

Measured, though owed to validate-slice. The oracle's source is now the yaml file alone and needs no interpreter. C-001 and C-003, each run alone with -Case, exit 0 under both powershell.exe and pwsh. The probe's shapes are all lone -Case runs under both shells.

Measured, though owed to validate-slice. After the engine appended SL-053's rule, `pwsh -File eng/rules-parity.ps1` prints 'rules-parity: AGREE 11 facts <- 15 twinned entries, 27 patterns; 33 settled entries not compared', exit 0. The entry landed as settled, and facts, twinned and patterns are unchanged.

deviations: Oracle source. The design derived ExpectedSettled from Fitness's rule count as Case-C007 obtains it, lifted into a shared function. The O-015 decision, which is newer and was made by a person, overrides that: leave Case-C007 exactly as it is and use a direct per-entry count of .taad/fitness.yaml instead. Reading the code backs the decision: C-007 gets the rule count from harness output ('fitness pass, (\d+) rules'), which needs -EnginePython and -EngineRoot, and lone C-001 and C-003 runs don't have those. What was built counts every item of the rules: list (list items at the list's own indent), not per marker, minus the pinned 15 twinned. That keeps the design's arithmetic (rule count minus twinned) with the count taken from the yaml, and it measures the same as Fitness (48). The decision text reached this build clipped at 220 characters, so any detail after 'direct per-entry count of .taad/fitn...' was not visible.

The probe is permanent, not a throwaway. The design called for a build-time probe that would be deleted. But obligations O-002 to O-011 must be discharged by a test command the engine runs after the build, and a deleted probe cannot run. It lives in its own script, tests/rules/SettledCountProbe.ps1, rather than as new RuleCases case IDs, so SL-031's case list gains no fixture machinery.

The probe's scratch copy holds only the four files C-001 and C-003 read (RuleCases.ps1, eng/rules-parity.ps1, .taad/fitness.yaml, ArchitectureRulesTests.cs), copied from the working tree, not the whole tree. That is enough for those cases, faster, and keeps the design's point that the uncommitted working tree is used rather than HEAD.

The twinned count is written once, as $Twinned = 15. Both AGREE lines interpolate it and the oracle subtracts it, so the pinned figure can't drift between the expected line and the oracle. It is still a literal, as the design required. Facts (11) and patterns (27) stay inline literals.
The error messages keep the design's prefixes ('ExpectedSettled: fitness rule count unavailable', 'ExpectedSettled: derived count <n> < 1') and add the reason, or the rules and twinned counts.
not_built: Case-C007 was not modified and its rule-count expression was not lifted into a shared function, as the O-015 decision directs. The design's 'Fitness rule-count source (shared with C-007)' component is therefore deliberately not built.
follow_ups: O-005 (from the SL-031 reflection) is still open: no engine gate runs tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1 or tests/rules/SettledCountProbe.ps1. For now the fitness guard rule is the only enforcement anyone will see. Wiring them into a gate is a process slice of its own.
SettledCountProbe -Shape GuardRule reads the pre-fix RuleCases.ps1 from commit 0647ead17aa99f2aace803624966ca4b1edab65b. If history is ever rewritten, that check fails loudly and needs a new anchor.
The C-007 test command (C-010 here) embeds machine-specific engine paths: %APPDATA%\taad3\venv\Scripts\python.exe and C:\Users\sshub\projets\taad_v3\backend.

Twinned (15), facts (11) and patterns (27) are still pinned in C-001, C-003, C-004 and C-005, and C-008 pins 14 and 15 twinned. That is deliberate per the design, but a slice that adds a twinned entry must hand-edit them.

The SL-053 guard rule's 'because' text in .taad/fitness.yaml says the count must come from 'the Fitness rule count minus the twinned count'. That is still accurate, since the direct count of rules: items equals Fitness's rule count (48 both ways), so it was not hand-edited.

tests.note: Exit 0, 3 s, 8 ok. Expected and seen: 'rules-parity: AGREE 11 facts <- 15 twinned entries, 27 patterns; 33 settled entries not compared' under powershell.exe and pwsh, with and without -ExpectFacts 11. Before the fix the same command exited 1 (28 expected, 32 or 33 seen).
Exit 0. The oracle evaluated under Windows PowerShell 5.1: same 33, 8 ok.
Exit 0, 6 s. The appended-entry check expects and sees 34 settled under both inner shells. The same run under powershell.exe also exits 0.

Exit 0, 96 s, all 9 shapes green: AppendOne 34, AppendTwo 35, CountPlusOne/NotAgree/Misclassified each exit 1 with 4 failed checks, C003Base green and 2 failed checks on each mutation, OracleUnavailable with the named messages and C-002 still green, BothShells 33 and 1, GuardRule 205,268 pre-fix and none post-fix.

Checks that the probe itself bites. With the pre-fix pinned RuleCases.ps1, AppendOne exits 1. With an oracle read back from parity output, CountPlusOne and C003Base exit 1. With an expected line read from the tool, Misclassified exits 1.
Exit 0, 52 s. Clean scenario CLEAN, 'the Fitness rule count equals the yaml entries (twinned + settled)' ok, and the stray-violation bite exits 2.
